packs.name: NZ Unit Titles Act 2010 + Regulations 2011 (body corporate)
recommended: Send BOTH notices for an AGM: notice of intention at least 3 weeks before (6 weeks for a parent development) to invite nominations, then the notice of meeting at least 2 weeks before (3 weeks for a parent development) (Regs 2011 regs 5-6).
A meeting called only to elect the chairperson or committee needs a notice of intention at least 2 weeks before (reg 7).
Offer remote attendance and electronic voting for every meeting and include the proxy and postal voting forms in the notice (Act ss 88(3), 103, 103A; regs 6, 12A, 15A).
A poll can be requested after any ordinary or special resolution and is then counted by ownership interest (Act ss 99-100); the product's per-flat count is only the first step.
Owners with unpaid levies cannot vote or count towards the quorum (Act s 96(3), s 95(1)(b)); keep the levy status list current.
gaps: Poll after a show of votes, counted by ownership interest, which can reverse the result (ss 99-100).
Special resolution needs 75% of those who vote; the product has no percentage setting for the special majority.
Quorum minimum of 2 persons when the body corporate has 2+ members (s 95(1A)).
Two-step AGM notice (intention + meeting) and parent-development longer notices.
Notice for an owner-requisitioned EGM must go out within 5 working days of the request and the meeting held within 3 weeks.
Postal and electronic votes are void for a motion that is materially amended at the meeting (regs 15, 15A).

packs.name: NZ incorporated society (residents' group) - enter your constitution values
recommended: Open the society's constitution and enter its notice period, quorum and majorities in the steps that follow: the Act leaves these to the constitution (Act ss 26(1)(k), 87(3)).
Proxy, postal and electronic voting are lawful only if the constitution says so (s 93).
gaps: The Act sets no numbers for notice, quorum or majorities, so nothing can be pre-filled.

packs.name: Queensland BCCM Act 1997 + Standard Module 2020
recommended: Every general meeting needs at least 21 days between giving notice and the meeting (Standard Module reg 91).
Committee elections are by secret ballot unless the body corporate decides on an open ballot by ordinary resolution (reg 15(3)); keep secret ballot on for elections.
Owners in debt cannot vote or stand (reg 102(2), reg 10(2)(d)): refresh the arrears list before the meeting.
Send the minutes to every owner within 21 days (reg 117(2)).
If the scheme has 20 or more lots, nobody may hold proxies for more than 5% of the lots; below 20 lots, one proxy only (reg 128(4)).
gaps: Special resolution has THREE tests (two-thirds of votes cast; against-votes at most 25% of lots; against-votes at most 25% of contribution entitlement); the product models only one majority base.
Poll counted by contribution-schedule lot entitlement, which can reverse a show-of-votes result.
Proxy cap depends on scheme size (5% of lots, or 1 if under 20 lots).
Adjourned-meeting quorum needs the chairperson (or authorised manager) present in person.
Quorum floor of 2 voters present personally.
Resolution without dissent and majority resolution (more than 50% of all lots, written, no proxy) have no product equivalent.
Weighting applies only on a poll, so the weightage option is left for the Organizer.

packs.name: Victoria Owners Corporations Act 2006
recommended: Give at least 14 days' written notice for the AGM and any special general meeting (Act ss 72, 76).
The AGM notice must carry the financial statements, the proposed budget, the previous minutes and a statement of the right to appoint a proxy (s 72(2)).
Proxy rule: no one may vote as proxy for more than 1 owner (20 or fewer occupiable lots) or 5% of owners (more than 20 lots) (s 89D).
Owners in arrears cannot vote except on special or unanimous resolutions (s 89B): check the arrears list.
A tie fails unless the chairperson is an owner or proxy and uses the casting vote (s 89A).
gaps: Quorum: 50% of lots OR, if that is not available, 50% of lot entitlement (two bases).
No quorum does not stop the meeting: its resolutions become interim and need confirmation after 29 days (s 78).
Special resolution: 75% of ALL votes/lot entitlement, plus interim special resolution (50% in favour, 25% or less against, 29-day petition) (ss 96-97).
Poll by lot entitlement on ordinary resolutions can overturn a show of hands (s 89(3),(5)).
Proxy cap depends on number of occupiable lots and has family exceptions.
Ballot (post/electronic decision without a meeting) with its own 14-day closing date.
Regulations 2018 (proxy form, teleconference, Schedule 2 model rules) were not read, so confidence is held at medium.

packs.name: ACT Unit Titles (Management) Act 2011
recommended: Give 14 days' notice; make it 21 days when a motion needs an unopposed or unanimous resolution (Sch 3 s 3.6(2)).
Include a proxy form and an absentee voting paper in every notice (s 3.7(2)).
Wait 30 minutes: a reduced quorum of 2 people can then decide, but the decision only takes effect after 28 days and can be disallowed by a majority petition (ss 3.9-3.11).
Proxy cap: 1 per person, or 5% of units when there are more than 20 units; the chairperson is exempt (s 3.26(3)).
Unit owners with money owing cannot vote on ordinary or special resolutions (s 3.20(3)).
gaps: Reduced quorum after 30 minutes and the 28-day disallow petition.
Special resolution test is 'for > against AND against <= 1/4 of votes that could be cast by people present'; there are 3-member and 1-2-member variants.
Unopposed and unanimous resolution types, with 21-day notice.
Absentee vote paper counts as present for voting but not for quorum.
Proxy cap by number of units (5% when above 20 units), with chairperson exemption.

packs.name: Western Australia Strata Titles Act 1985 (2018 reforms)
recommended: Give at least 14 days' notice of every general meeting, and list every accepted voting method including electronic ones (Act s 129).
A special, unanimous or without-dissent resolution needs 14 days' notice of its exact wording (s 123).
If no quorum after 30 minutes, those present are the quorum, but in 2-lot schemes all owners must be present (s 130).
A sole-owner individual who attends must vote personally, not by proxy (s 125(1)).
Owners with outstanding recoverable amounts cannot vote except on unanimous or without-dissent resolutions (s 120(3)).
gaps: Special resolution has FOUR tests (50% of lots and 50% of unit entitlements in favour; under 25% of each against), and small-scheme variants.
Votes on special, unanimous or without-dissent resolutions remain open for 28 days after the meeting (s 121).
Quorum falls back to 'whoever is present' after 30 minutes inside the same meeting.
A demand can switch an ordinary resolution from a count by number to a count by unit entitlement (s 122).
Proxy limits for strata managers depend on Regulations not read.

packs.name: Northern Territory Unit Title Schemes Act 2009 + Management Module 1
recommended: Allow at least 14 WORKING days between notice and the meeting (21 working days if a resolution without dissent, unanimous resolution or termination is on the agenda) (Module 1 cl 32).
Attach the annual financial statement and budget to the AGM notice, and the text of every special/without-dissent/unanimous motion (cl 32(2)).
A lot owner with unpaid levies cannot vote except on unanimous or without-dissent resolutions (Act s 79(9),(10)).
A chair who is also a voter may cast an extra deciding vote on a tied ordinary resolution (cl 38).
gaps: Notice in working days (14 or 21), not calendar days: notice.minDays and the notice table are left empty on purpose.
Interim resolutions when there is no quorum, with confirmation within 28-29 working days (cls 3, 34).
Special resolution needs two-thirds of votes cast AND at most 25% of contribution entitlements against.
Absentee voting exists only for without-dissent and unanimous resolutions.
Resolution types: majority resolution (over 50% of all units), unanimous resolution (all units), without dissent.

packs.name: Tasmania Strata Titles Act 1998
recommended: Give written notice at least 7 days before any general meeting, with the business and, for a unanimous resolution, its exact terms (Act s 75(4)).
Check the scheme's own by-laws: they can require longer notice and a different quorum than Schedule 1 by-law 10.
A unanimous resolution stays open for 28 days after the meeting for written votes (s 78).
gaps: Unanimous resolution (no dissent, 28-day written voting window).
Show of hands by member versus poll by unit entitlement; co-owner rules (s 76).
No statutory term, election procedure, electronic voting or proxy rules; the body corporate's by-laws decide.

packs.name: South Australia Community Titles Act 1996 (secondary-source summary)
recommended: Give at least 14 days' written notice with the agenda; special and unanimous resolutions must be set out in full in the notice (CTA s 81).
Pick a day, time and place that suit most members (s 81(3)).
Absentee votes must reach the secretary at least 6 hours before the meeting (s 84(11)). All of these values come from a summary, not the Act: check the Act.
gaps: Special resolution: at most 25% of the total possible votes against (small-lot variants for 2-3 lots), not a majority of those present.
Unanimous resolution (no dissent; absentees not counted).
Adjourned meeting must be 7-14 days later with written notice.
Requisition by 20% of entitlements OR 20% of lots (either).

packs.name: South Australia Strata Titles Act 1988 (secondary-source summary)
recommended: Give 14 days' written notice with the agenda; special and unanimous resolutions must be set out in full in the notice (STA s 33(3),(4a)).
Absentee votes must reach the secretary at least 6 hours before (s 34(4)).
gaps: Special resolution: at most 25% of total possible votes against; unanimous resolution variant.
Adjourned meeting must be 7-14 days later.
Requisition by one-fifth of unit holders (basis unclear).

packs.name: New South Wales Strata Schemes Management Act 2015 (guidance-based)
recommended: AGM needs 14 days' written notice; any other general meeting 7 days (NSW Government strata meetings guidance).
Name every voting method (remote, pre-meeting electronic) in the notice; pre-meeting electronic voting needs a resolution first and cannot elect the strata committee.
Send minutes to all owners within 7 days.
Unpaid-levy owners cannot vote except on unanimous motions.
gaps: Quorum is met by EITHER 25% of the people entitled to vote OR 25% of unit entitlements: the quorum basis is left for the Organizer to choose.
Special resolution: no more than 25% of the unit-entitlement vote against; the product's special-majority setting does not model a cap on 'against' votes.
Sustainability/accessibility infrastructure resolutions (less than 50% against).
Poll switches the count from per-lot to unit entitlement.
Mortgagee priority votes.
Proxy limits depend on scheme size (20 lots / 5%).
Primary text unread: confidence stays medium.

packs.name: Ontario Condominium Act, 1998 + O. Reg. 48/01

weightage.reason: Condominium Act, 1998 s.51(2): all voting by owners is one vote per unit

proxy_voting.reason: Condominium Act, 1998 s.52(3),(4): a proxy may vote and need not be an owner

recommended: s.47(1)(b): send written notice at least 15 days before any owners' meeting; s.47(1)(c) a preliminary notice must go out at least 20 days before that notice.
s.50(1): quorum is 25% of units; at an AGM the third attempt only needs 15% (s.50(1.1)).
s.49: owners 30+ days in arrears cannot vote unless they pay before the meeting.
s.52(1.1): the by-laws may limit electronic meetings/voting; read them before choosing 'online'.
s.55 and O. Reg. 48/01 s.13.1: keep the minute book for ever and ballots/proxies at least 90 days.
gaps: Preliminary notice 20 days before the notice of meeting, and candidate nomination deadline set in it.
Third-attempt 15% quorum (the product cannot count attempts).
Arrears of 30+ days remove the right to vote (defaulter rule).
Parking/storage units have no vote; joint owners split 50/50 are not counted.
Owner-occupier reserved board seat (voted only by owner-occupiers).
Director removal by more than 50% of ALL units; other special thresholds.
Different retention periods per record type (permanent / 7 years / 90 days).

packs.name: British Columbia Strata Property Act + Standard Bylaws

proxy_voting.reason: Strata Property Act s.56(1): a person who may vote can vote in person or by proxy

recommended: s.45(1): give at least 2 weeks' written notice; mailed or e-mailed notice counts as given only 4 days after sending (s.61(3)), so send early.
s.48(2)-(3): quorum is 1/3 of the votes; if it fails, adjourn to the same time next week and then whoever is there forms the quorum.
Standard Bylaw 27(7): if any eligible voter asks, the council election and any other vote must be by secret ballot (not for people attending electronically, Act s.49(3)).
s.28 and bylaw 10: council is elected every AGM; owners, corporate representatives and assigned tenants may stand.
gaps: 3/4, 80% and unanimous thresholds (the product has no threshold setting).
Strata corporations with a Schedule of Voting Rights (unit entitlement votes) versus one vote per lot.
Secret ballot only on request by an eligible voter (not a plain yes/no).
Reconsideration meeting (25% demand within a week after a 3/4 vote by under 50% of votes).
Tie casting vote exists only if bylaws provide it (standard bylaws do).
Waiver of the AGM by written consent of all voters.

packs.name: Alberta Condominium Property Act + default bylaws (Reg Sched. 4)

proxy_voting.reason: Condominium Property Act s.26(4): an owner may vote personally or by proxy

recommended: s.30(3): written notice to every owner at least 14 days before; also send statements, reserve report and budget 14 days before an AGM.
Default bylaw 20: quorum is 25% of persons entitled to notice; if missed, same day next week and then those present form the quorum.
Proxy rules (Reg ss.31.2-31.5): valid 6 months at most; not to a manager or employee except to make quorum; latest proxy wins.
If your corporation has its own registered bylaws they replace the defaults above (Act s.33) - check them first.
gaps: Special resolution needs 75% of persons AND 75% of unit factors (two-part test).
Owner vote versus unit-factor vote, which any voter can demand before results are announced.
Proxies expire after 6 months; manager/employee proxy only for quorum.
Preliminary notice 60 days before the AGM with agenda-item call (default bylaw 19).
Written-resolution route instead of a meeting (s.26(6)).

packs.name: Quebec divided co-ownership (CCQ arts. 1038 ff.) - verify before use
recommended: Secondary source only: check arts. 346, 352, 1089, 1090 in LegisQuebec before relying on these numbers.
Read your declaration of co-ownership: it may set a different notice period or voting split.
gaps: Adjourned-meeting quorum (sources conflict).
Majorities of 50% of owners AND 75%/90% of votes (two-part tests).
Vote reduction rules (small buildings, developer cap, 3-month arrears).
Secret ballot on request.
Annual meeting deadline and electronic meetings: not verified.

packs.name: Manitoba Condominium Act (C.C.S.M. c. C170)

proxy_voting.reason: The Condominium Act (MB) s.120: a right to vote may be exercised in person or by proxy

recommended: s.116: the notice must be written, say where/when/what business, and carry any proposed by-law changes; the number of days is NOT in the Act - take it from your by-laws or the regulations.
s.117-118: quorum is 33% of voting rights (66% if under 4 units or owners); a failed meeting can be adjourned and then those present are the quorum.
s.128: a manager, the corporation's employees or agents cannot hold an owner's proxy.
gaps: Notice day count (outside the Act).
66% quorum for corporations with fewer than 4 units/owners.
80% written-consent matters and 30-day notice for them.
Optional arrears bar on voting by by-law (clause 167(1)(y)).

packs.name: Saskatchewan Condominium Property Act, 1993 + default bylaws

proxy_voting.reason: Condominium Property Act, 1993 s.41.1: an owner may appoint a proxy (standing proxy max 6 months)

recommended: Default bylaw 21: at least 7 days' written notice with the business and the level of approval each item needs.
s.41(10): owners 30+ days in arrears must be warned in writing at least 10 days before the meeting that they cannot vote unless they pay.
s.41.1: a standing proxy lasts at most 6 months; the manager and corporation employees cannot be proxies.
If the corporation passed its own bylaws these defaults no longer apply.
gaps: Special resolution = two-thirds of persons entitled to vote (no threshold setting).
Default show of hands vs vote by unit factors on demand.
Arrears bar on voting and the 10-day warning (Act s.41(8)-(11)).
6-month proxy expiry.
Tie: show-of-hands tie goes to a unit-factor vote.

packs.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Condominium Act, 2009

weightage.reason: Condominium Act, 2009 (NL) s.21(1): all voting by owners is on the basis of one vote per unit

proxy_voting.reason: Condominium Act, 2009 (NL) s.21(1): voting may be done by proxy

recommended: s.20: quorum is owners of at least 30% of the common elements, present or by proxy; if short, adjourn to a fixed time and place.
s.21(6): electronic votes must be verifiable but must not show how any member voted.
s.27(4): a board term is up to 3 years unless the by-laws shorten it.
gaps: Meeting notice period and owner requisition: not in the Act text read.
Quorum counts the share of common elements (interest), but voting is one vote per unit.
Declarant-appointed directors while the declarant owns units.

packs.name: Prince Edward Island Condominium Act (c.C-16)
recommended: s.11(5): give at least ten days' written notice, with place, date, hour and business.
s.11(3): owners of 25% of the common elements can force a meeting; if the board does not act in 30 days they can call it themselves.
The Act sets no quorum or proxy rule: enter the values from your declaration or by-laws.
gaps: Quorum, proxies, voting majority for ordinary items: left to declaration/by-laws.
66 2/3% of common elements for by-laws; 80% for some alterations (no threshold setting).
Directors removable by members owning a majority of units.

packs.name: Northwest Territories Condominium Act (mirror-sourced)
recommended: The Act leaves notice, quorum, requisition and board term to the declaration and by-laws (s.16): enter those values from your own documents.
s.16.2: hold the AGM within 6 months of year end and send financial statements and budget at least 7 days before it.
s.20(5): owners more than 30 days in arrears cannot vote.
gaps: Special resolution = 66 2/3% of common elements (no threshold setting).
Voting weight from the declaration, default by share of common elements.
Arrears bar on voting.
Developer-controlled board until it owns under 80% of the common elements.

recommended: RERA only says the association of allottees must be formed (s.11(4)(e), default 3 months after a majority of allottees book) and receive the common areas (s.17). Use the State pack for notice, quorum and election rules.
Until the association takes over, the promoter must maintain essential services (s.11(4)(d)) - keep proof of the handover date in the minutes.
gaps: RERA sets no meeting or election rules, so this pack carries no notice, quorum or voting settings; choose the State pack for those.
Per-State RERA rules that DO fix an association timeline or model bye-laws (e.g. State RERA rules) were not read for the states in this file.
packs.name: Central layer: RERA 2016 (association of allottees) - applies on top of the State regime

recommended: s.16(2)(b): if the bye-laws set no other quorum percentage, the quorum is a majority of owners; 'majority' means 51% or more of the votes under the Declaration (s.3(n)). Check your registered bye-laws first - they override this default.
Votes follow the percentages written in the Declaration (s.11(1)(f)), not one-flat-one-vote, unless your Declaration says otherwise.
s.16(2)(a): at least one-third of the Board must retire every year (s.16(2)(a)).
The Act is silent on notice days, proxies and secret ballot - enter what your bye-laws say.
gaps: Act fixes no notice period, AGM date, requisition share or proxy rule - all in the society's own bye-laws (not read).
One-third-of-Board-retires-every-year staggered terms cannot be expressed as a single 'term years' setting.
Whether 'majority of owners' for quorum means 51% of votes or 51% of heads is an inference from s.3(n) - lawyer check advised.
packs.name: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act 1972 (association of apartment owners + own bye-laws)

recommended: s.21(1): members vote in person, not by proxy. Section 20(1): one member, one vote.
s.28A(3): in every primary society one committee seat is reserved for SC/ST and one for women, unless there is no eligible member.
s.27(1): hold the annual general meeting before 30 September (Registrar can extend by up to six months).
Notice days and quorum are in your registered bye-laws / the 1960 Rules - not read; enter them yourself.
gaps: Special-meeting requisition is 'fifty members or one-fifth of members, whichever is less' (s.28(1)); the product has only a single percentage setting.
Committee term text shows 5 co-operative years; office-bearer term shorter (President/Chair 2.5 years s.29F(5)) - not separately expressible.
Elections are supervised by the Registrar / State election authority under Chapter VA - the product cannot model an external election authority.
packs.name: Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act 1959 (co-operative housing society)

recommended: s.11: hold the first AGM within 18 months of registration and later AGMs within 9 months after the end of the year in which the previous AGM was held (Registrar can extend by up to 6 months).

s.11: a special general meeting can be requested by the president, one-third of the governing body, or one-tenth of voting members; governing body must act within 10 days and hold the meeting within 40 days.
The Act sets no notice period and no quorum - these come from the society's own bye-laws.
s.13: file the member list and audited accounts within 14 days after the AGM.
gaps: Act has no notice days, quorum, proxy or election rules - all left to the society's bye-laws (not read).
AGM deadlines (18 / 9 months) and the 10/40-day special-meeting timetable are not expressible in the product's settings.
packs.name: Karnataka Societies Registration Act 1960 (RWA / AOA registered as a society)

recommended: Model by-law 16: notice of owners' meetings must go out at least 2 and at most 7 days before - unusually short; check your registered bye-laws.
Model by-law 11: votes are cast in person, no proxy. By-law 9: votes follow the percentage in the Declaration.
Model by-law 10: quorum is a majority of owners present in person; by-law 17: an adjourned meeting must be at least 48 hours later and any two owners present in person form its quorum.
By-law 8: owners more than 60 days in arrears at year end cannot vote in office elections or stand for office.
By-law 23: Board Managers serve 3 years; by-law 56: bye-laws are amended by owners representing at least 75% of total value.
gaps: Business outside the notice at a special meeting needs four-fifths of owners present in person (by-law 15) - no setting for this.
75% of value to amend bye-laws and 60-day arrears bar cannot be expressed.
Quorum 'majority of owners' read as 51% of votes (by-law 2(f) definition); a head-count reading is possible - lawyer check.
packs.name: Haryana Apartment Ownership Act 1983 + Rules 1987 model bye-laws (Exhibit B)

recommended: s.31: give 14 clear days notice of every general meeting and endorse a copy to the District Registrar.
s.29(3): quorum is at least 40% of members entitled to vote, present in person, and never fewer than four.
s.31(6): the governing body must call an extraordinary meeting within 45 days of a requisition by one-tenth of members.
s.29(4): one member, one vote, cast in person.
gaps: Special resolution = 3/5 of those present and voting with 40% quorum (s.2(xxiv)) - the product has no setting for the 3/5 figure.
Governing body term is 'not more than three years' (s.33(3)); a maximum, not a fixed term, so not set.
Voting rights require payment of dues (s.20(2)) - no defaulter setting.
Where a Collegium is required (more than 300 members, s.30) votes are exercised by it - not modelled.
packs.name: Haryana Registration and Regulation of Societies Act 2012 (RWA / society)

recommended: s.20: one member, one vote; chairman has a casting vote on a tie. s.21: members vote in person, no proxy.
s.28(1): each committee must include at least one SC member and one woman; a backward-class seat also if that class is 10% or more of members.
s.28(3)-(4): committee term five years; elections must be arranged before it ends, else the Registrar holds them within 90 days.
Notice days and quorum are left to the bye-laws (s.9A(2)(xvii)-(xviii)) - enter what your bye-laws say.
gaps: Requisition share is whatever the bye-laws say (s.26(1)), so no percentage is set.
Notice and quorum are bye-law matters; model bye-laws not read.
packs.name: Haryana Co-operative Societies Act 1984 (co-operative housing society)

recommended: Part I (s.10): the promoter must apply to the Registrar to form a co-operative society or company once enough flat-takers have joined - after that, meetings follow the Gujarat Co-operative Societies Act (see in-gj-coop-act).
Part II (apartment ownership): s.31(2)(b) bye-laws must state how owners' meetings are called and the quorum if not a majority; s.31(2)(k) the percentage of votes to amend bye-laws.
gaps: No numbers: the Act text read gives no notice period, quorum figure or voting percentage; the definition of 'majority' in the Gujarat Act was not read.
Gujarat Ownership Flats Rules and any model bye-laws not read.
packs.name: Gujarat Ownership Flats Act 1973 (society / company / association of apartment owners)

recommended: s.28(1): each member has one vote and the Chairman has a casting vote on a tie. Joint holders: only the first-named holder votes (s.28(2)).
s.74(1C): committee term is five years from election (the shorter 3-year term in s.74C(2) applies only to listed apex/bank/sugar-type societies).

s.77: hold the AGM within six months of the financial year end. s.78: committee must call a special meeting within one month of a requisition by one-fifth of members or the lower number in the bye-laws.
Notice days and quorum: not read; use your registered bye-laws.
gaps: Reserved seats: one for SC/ST and two for women only in societies of individual members that have such members (s.74(1B)); conditional, so not set as a fixed number.
Proxy rule not read (s.28 text shows no proxy language) - left undecided.
Requisition is 'one-fifth or the lower number in the bye-laws' - the product can hold only one percentage.
packs.name: Gujarat Co-operative Societies Act 1961 (co-operative housing society)

recommended: s.18(2)(b): bye-laws must say how owners' meetings are called and the quorum - the Act gives no figure, so copy yours from the registered bye-laws.
Voting follows the percentage of undivided interest in the Declaration 'for all purposes, including voting' (s.14(1)(f)).
gaps: Act gives no notice period, quorum, majority or term figures at all; Rules and any model bye-laws not read.
packs.name: Andhra Pradesh Apartments (Promotion of Construction and Ownership) Act 1987 (association of apartment owners)

proxy_voting.reason: Goa Co-operative Societies Act s.28(1): every right to vote is exercised personally, not by proxy (only a defence-services member may vote by proxy)

recommended: s.28(1): vote in person, no proxy (only a Defence Services member may vote through another member); the chairman has a casting vote on a tie.
s.72(2): hold the AGM within nine months of the close of the co-operative year, and never more than fifteen months after the previous AGM.
s.58A / s.72(3): the board must call a general meeting within one month (s.58A) / thirty days (s.72(3)) of a requisition by one-tenth of members.

Rule 46(6): if a meeting fails for want of quorum it is adjourned to a later time the same day or to a date not earlier than 7 days, and the original agenda is then transacted whether there is a quorum or not.

s.59(2)-(3): board term five years; at most 15 directors. s.66(3): board election is by secret ballot (elections by the Registrar for societies with paid-up capital of Rs 25 lakh or more; smaller societies follow their own bye-laws and election rules, s.66(5)).
s.72(7): the chair signs the general meeting minutes within 30 days; s.72(6): minutes go to everyone invited within 45 days.
gaps: Notice days and quorum figure are set by the society's registered bye-laws (rule 46(2)) - not read.
Rule 46(6): the adjourned meeting may be on the same day (later hour) OR a date at least 7 days later; the product's 'minimum hours later' cannot express the same-day option, so left unset.
Election of directors must be by secret ballot (s.66(3)) but the product's secret-ballot option is set per event, so left for the Organizer.
Records: minute books and members' register must be kept permanently, other books 8 years (rule 47) - 'permanent' cannot be expressed.
Rule 46(3) ordinary resolutions: show of hands by majority of members present - 'show of hands' not a product setting.
packs.name: Goa Co-operative Societies Act 2001 + Rules 2003 (co-operative housing society)

recommended: s.16: the bye-laws (framed by the competent authority with State approval, per a summary) must cover how the Board is elected, retirement of members each year, how owners' meetings are called and the quorum - get the actual bye-laws from the competent authority.

packs.name: Himachal Pradesh Apartment Ownership Act 1978 (association of apartment owners)

An owner in arrears 3 days before the meeting cannot vote (except on unanimous / consensus resolutions) - publish the list of persons entitled to vote on the notice board 48 hours before (para 7).
Display minutes within 45 days for at least 14 days (Second Schedule para 3).
Written council nominations must reach the secretary 48 hours before the meeting (s.53B).

42-1903.05(g): the executive board must approve any electronic voting process.
gaps: Quorum is more than 33 1/3%; set as 3333 bp strict (rounding error under 0.004%)
Witnessed-signature requirement for proxies not a setting
Notice minimum differs: 21 days (annual/regular) vs 7 days (other)
Proxy expiry at first meeting not a setting

packs.name: Wyoming Nonprofit Corporation Act (W.S. 17-19-101 et seq.) - default for incorporated HOAs / condominium associations
recommended: W.S. 17-19-705: give members notice of place, date and time 10 to 60 days before every meeting.
W.S. 17-19-722: unless your bylaws say otherwise, 10% of the votes is a quorum.
W.S. 17-19-724: proxies run 11 months unless the form says otherwise, never more than 3 years; articles/bylaws may limit them.
W.S. 17-19-702: 5% of the voting power can demand a special meeting.
gaps: Ordinary resolutions also need a majority of the required quorum: not expressible
Below one-third attendance only noticed matters may be voted: not expressible

packs.name: Wyoming Condominium Ownership Act (W.S. 34-20-101 to 34-20-104)
recommended: Wyoming's condominium Act sets no notice, quorum or proxy rules; copy them from your declaration/bylaws (or the Nonprofit Corporation Act if incorporated).
gaps: No statutory numbers at all

packs.name: Nevada Common-Interest Ownership (NRS chapter 116) - HOAs, condominiums, co-operatives
recommended: NRS 116.3108(3): notice of every owners' meeting 15 to 60 days ahead, with the agenda.
NRS 116.3109: quorum is 20% of the votes (proxy and absentee votes count) unless your documents set more.
NRS 116.31034(15): electing board members needs a SECRET WRITTEN BALLOT mailed at least 15 days before counting; candidates and sitting board members must not handle the ballots; no quorum is needed.
NRS 116.311(6): proxies may NOT be used to elect or remove a board member - keep proxies off for election points.
NRS 116.3108(5): make meeting minutes (or a summary) available within 30 days.
gaps: Secret ballot and the proxy ban apply to board elections/removals only; the product's options are per event, not per point type
Absentee ballot request deadline (3 days) and ballot-without-meeting rules not expressible
Board-term maximum (3 years) and staggering shown as a number only
Executive board meeting cadence (quarterly) not expressible

packs.name: South Dakota Nonprofit Corporation Act (SDCL chs. 47-22 to 47-28) - default for incorporated HOAs / condominium associations
recommended: SDCL 47-23-7: notice 10 to 50 days before every members' meeting unless your articles or bylaws say otherwise.
SDCL 47-23-12: one-tenth of the votes is a quorum unless your bylaws set another figure.
SDCL 47-23-9: proxies are allowed unless your articles or bylaws bar them, and last 11 months at most unless stated.
SDCL 47-23-5: unless your bylaws set a figure, members with one-twentieth of the votes can call a special meeting.
gaps: Majority is 'majority of votes of members present or represented'; engine basis 'present' approximates it
Ballot-without-meeting rules not expressible

packs.name: North Carolina Planned Community Act (N.C.G.S. ch. 47F)
recommended: 47F-3-108: give notice 10 to 60 days before every owners' meeting, with the agenda.
47F-3-109: quorum is 10% of the votes unless your bylaws say otherwise; if a meeting fails for lack of quorum the next one needs half as much.
47F-3-110: a proxy must be dated and ends 11 months after its date unless it says less; check the 1999 applicability limits for older communities.
gaps: Halving of quorum at each adjourned meeting is not a setting
Applicability limits for pre-1999 communities cannot be expressed
All values rest on secondary sources: have a North Carolina lawyer confirm

packs.name: North Carolina Condominium Act (N.C.G.S. ch. 47C)
recommended: Ch. 47C appears to give 10-60 days notice, 20% quorum, 1-year proxies, but this is from one summary only: confirm in your bylaws and the statute.
gaps: Everything unverified against the statute

packs.name: New Jersey Planned Real Estate Development Full Disclosure Act election rules (N.J.S.A. 45:22A-45.2 + N.J.A.C. 5:26-8) - HOAs and condominium associations
recommended: 45:22A-45.2: election notice 14 to 60 days before the election meeting, with the ballot and proxy/absentee forms attached (associations of 50+ units).
45:22A-45.2: proxies may only be used in a board election if absentee ballots are also offered.
45:22A-45.2: owners in good standing may nominate any member in good standing; give 30 days' notice of the nomination right before the election notice and at least 14 days for nominations.
If your documents set no election timing, the board must be elected every 2 years.
gaps: Small-association (<50 units) 14-30 day rule not expressible
Quorum is set by each association's documents (nonprofit act default not read)
Rules for who may be on the board per unit not expressible

packs.name: New Jersey Condominium Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8B)
recommended: Copy notice, quorum and proxy rules from your bylaws; the Condominium Act leaves them to the bylaws. For board elections the 45:22A-45.2 pack also applies.
gaps: No statutory numbers verified

packs.name: Utah Community Association Act (Utah Code 57-8a) + Condominium Ownership Act (57-8) + Revised Nonprofit Corporation Act (16-6a)
recommended: Utah's Act leaves notice, quorum and election mechanics to your bylaws; copy them from there. The nonprofit-act fallback of 10-60 days is from one summary only.
gaps: No verified statutory numbers

packs.name: Ohio Condominium Property Law (R.C. ch. 5311)
recommended: R.C. 5311.08(B): your bylaws must state the notice procedure and quorum; the statute gives no numbers. At least one-fifth of the board terms must expire every year.
gaps: Staggered terms (one-fifth per year) not expressible
Statute provides no numbers - all in bylaws

packs.name: Ohio Planned Community Law (R.C. ch. 5312)
recommended: R.C. 5312.04: the board must call an owners' meeting every year; notice and quorum come from your declaration/bylaws.
gaps: No verified numbers

packs.name: Nebraska Condominium Property Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-825 et seq.) + Nonprofit Corporation Act default
recommended: 76-866 (per two summaries): notice 10 to 50 days before an owners' meeting, hand-delivered or mailed.
gaps: Quorum (35%?) and proxy terms are single-source and left out
Nonprofit-act citations conflict between sources

packs.name: New Hampshire Condominium Act (RSA 356-B)
recommended: RSA 356-B:37-a: notice 21 days before an annual or regularly scheduled meeting, 7 days before any other meeting.
RSA 356-B:38: quorum is more than one-third of the votes unless the bylaws set a lower figure (not below 25%).
RSA 356-B:39: proxy limits depend on the size of the condominium; check them in your bylaws.
gaps: Notice minimum differs for annual (21) and other (7) meetings
Proxy cap per holder (10% of votes cast for >20 units) not expressible as a count
Small-condominium quorum (greater of 3 persons or >33%) not expressible

packs.name: New Mexico Homeowner Association Act (NMSA 47-16)
recommended: 47-16-17(B): notice of every member meeting 10 to 50 days ahead (electronic, hand or mail); board meetings at least 48 hours ahead.
47-16-9 (per one summary): the association must offer in-person, absentee and proxy voting.
gaps: Quorum is left to community documents
Proxy/absentee mandatory-offer rule is single-source; verify before relying

packs.name: New Mexico Condominium Act (NMSA 47-7A to 47-7D; UCIOA-style 47-7C)
recommended: 47-7C-8: notice 10 to 60 days before owners' meetings; 47-7C-9: quorum is 20% of the votes unless your bylaws say otherwise.
gaps: Proxy terms single-source and left out

packs.name: Oklahoma Unit Ownership Estate Act (60 O.S. 501 et seq.) + General Corporation Act nonstock provisions (18 O.S.)
recommended: Oklahoma's statute leaves notice and quorum to the bylaws: copy them from there.
gaps: No verified numbers

packs.name: Rhode Island Condominium Act (R.I. Gen. Laws 34-36.1) + Nonprofit Corporation Act default (7-6)
recommended: 34-36.1-3.08: notice 10 to 60 days before owners' meetings; email only with the owner's written consent.
gaps: Quorum (20%) and proxy terms are single-source and left out

packs.name: Tennessee Condominium Act of 2008 (T.C.A. 66-27-201 et seq.) + Nonprofit Corporation Act default (48-51 to 48-68)
recommended: 66-27-408: notice 10 to 60 days before owners' meetings; 66-27-409: quorum 20% of the votes unless your bylaws say otherwise (2008 Act condominiums only).
gaps: Applies only to condominiums under the 2008 Act; HOAs follow documents + nonprofit act

packs.name: Vermont Common Interest Ownership Act (27A V.S.A.)
recommended: 27A V.S.A. 3-108: notice 10 to 60 days before any owners' meeting, with the agenda.
gaps: Quorum (20%), proxy cap (15%) single-source and left out

packs.name: West Virginia Uniform Common Interest Ownership Act (W. Va. Code 36B)
recommended: 36B-3-108: notice 10 to 60 days before any meeting.
gaps: Quorum and proxy terms single-source and left out

packs.name: Wisconsin Condominium Ownership Act (Wis. Stat. ch. 703) + nonstock corporation default (ch. 181)
recommended: Wis. Stat. 703.15: at least 10 days' written notice of owners' meetings.
Wis. Stat. 703.15(4)(d): a condominium proxy lasts at most 180 days - check this against your bylaws.
gaps: 180-day proxy limit not a setting
Quorum left to bylaws

packs.name: Germany: Wohnungseigentumsgesetz (WEG, reformed 2020), Eigentuemerversammlung
recommended: WEG s.24(4): send the invitation in text form at least 3 weeks ahead (a 'should', so shorter is lawful only if especially urgent).
WEG s.24(2): the administrator must call a meeting when MORE than a quarter of the owners demand it in text form with reasons.
WEG s.23(2): every item to be voted must be named in the invitation.
WEG s.25(3): a proxy must be in text form.
WEG s.25(4): an owner cannot vote on a deal or lawsuit between the community and that owner.
gaps: Resolution register (Beschluss-Sammlung) and the rule that a resolution is void if the subject was not in the invitation are not expressible.
One-vote-per-owner is the legal default but the owners' agreement can change it; weightage left false.
Requisition is 'more than' 25%, engine value is 25%.

packs.name: South Africa: Sectional Titles Schemes Management Act 8 of 2011 + Management Rules (Annexure 1, 2016)
recommended: Rule 15(1): give 14 days' written notice with agenda, summary of documents and the proxy form. Rule 15(7) allows 7 days only if trustees record urgency.
Rule 7(2): trustee nominations are due in writing, with consent, 48 hours before the AGM.
Rule 20(5)-(6): proxies are due 48 hours before the meeting; a managing agent or its staff cannot be a proxy.
Rule 19: schemes with fewer than 4 sections need two-thirds of votes for a quorum; set quorum to 6667 in that case.
Rule 17(1): hold the AGM within 4 months of financial year end.
gaps: Quorum is 33.33% generally but 66.67% for schemes with fewer than 4 sections: one value only.
Adjourned quorum is 'those present' after 30 minutes; engine has no 30-minute rule.
Special (usually 75%) and unanimous resolutions are defined in the Act (not read); majority.special not set.
Arrears vote-bar only after a court/adjudicator order, and not for special/unanimous resolutions: not expressible.
Special resolution passed by less than 50% triggers a one-week delay and a 25% re-vote demand: not expressible.
Developer's votes excluded from quorum: not expressible.

packs.name: France: Loi n 65-557 du 10 juillet 1965 (copropriete) + Decret n 67-223 du 17 mars 1967
recommended: Service-public: send the convocation at least 21 days before the assembly (unless urgent, or the regulation sets longer).
Service-public: send the minutes within one month; opposing or absent co-owners have 2 months to contest.
gaps: Statute text unavailable: quorum, proxy cap, requisition share, term of syndic and double-majority thresholds all left blank.
The article 24 / 25 / 26 majority ladder (present vs all owners vs two-thirds of all votes) is not fully expressible with one simple/special pair.

packs.name: Spain: Ley 49/1960 de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH), Junta de Propietarios
recommended: LPH art.16(3): give at least 6 days' notice of the annual meeting.
LPH art.16(2): if the first call lacks the majority of owners and shares, hold a second call (half an hour later or within 8 days with 3 days' notice).
LPH art.15(2): owners with overdue debts cannot vote.
LPH art.19(3): sign the minutes within 10 natural days.
gaps: Quorum and majority need BOTH a majority of owners and a majority of shares; engine counts only one basis.
Three-fifths and unanimity majorities (art.17) have no parameter.
Defaulter vote-ban with court-deposit exception not expressible.

packs.name: Brazil: Codigo Civil arts 1331 ff. (condominio edilicio) - assembleia de condominos
recommended: CC art.1354: every owner must be convened, otherwise the assembly cannot decide.
CC art.1355: one quarter of owners may call an extraordinary assembly.
CC art.1354-A: an electronic assembly is allowed unless the convention forbids it; say so in the notice and explain how to log in and vote.
Check the convention for the notice period and for proxy rules.
gaps: Notice days come from the convention, not the Code: Organizer must enter them.
Permanent session (60/90 days) is not expressible.
Quorum is 'majority of those present who hold at least half the fractions': two tests.

packs.name: Colombia: Ley 675 de 2001, Regimen de propiedad horizontal - asamblea general
recommended: Ley 675 art.39: the administrator calls the ordinary assembly with at least 15 calendar days' notice.
Ley 675 art.41: say in the first notice that a second call follows on the third business day with a plural number of owners.
Ley 675 art.42: a non-presential assembly needs provable records (sender, content, time, copy of the convocation).
gaps: Notice is in calendar days; second-call timing is business days: neither expressible exactly.
No-majority-above-70% cap is not expressible.

packs.name: Philippines: Magna Carta for Homeowners and Homeowners' Associations (RA 9904) - HOA meetings and elections
recommended: RA 9904 s.16: a proxy must be written, signed, and filed with the secretary before the meeting.
RA 9904 s.15(d): directors serve at most two years; read the by-laws for notice and quorum.
RA 9904 s.22(d): do not bar members in good standing from meetings or elections.
gaps: The Act delegates notice, quorum and majorities to by-laws: Organizer must enter by-law values.
Proxy 3-year validity cap not expressible.

packs.name: Philippines: Condominium Act (RA 4726) - condominium corporation / association of unit owners
recommended: RA 4726 s.9: notice, quorum and majorities come from the declaration of restrictions: copy them from yours.
gaps: Nearly everything is delegated to the declaration and the Corporation Code (not read).

packs.name: Japan: Act on Building Unit Ownership (Act No. 69 of 1962) - unit owners' meeting
recommended: Act art.35: send notice with the agenda at least 1 week ahead (the bylaws may change this).
Act art.37: only items named in the notice can be voted.
Act art.34(3): one-fifth of votes and one-fifth of owners can demand a meeting.
Act art.39(2): written votes and proxies are allowed; art.39(3): electronic voting needs a bylaw or meeting resolution.
Act art.42: written minutes are signed by the chair and two attending owners.
gaps: Every decision needs a majority of owners AND a majority of votes (dual test); engine has one basis.
Requisition needs two one-fifth tests.
Bylaws change needs 3/4 of owners and 3/4 of votes: no parameter.
Bylaws can override notice period and electronic voting.

packs.name: UAE (Dubai): Law No. 6 of 2019 - Owners Committee of jointly owned property
recommended: Law 6/2019 art.23(a): an Owners Committee meeting is valid only if a majority of members attend and the chairman or vice chairman is there.
Law 6/2019 art.23(c): one vote per member; the chair breaks a tie.
Law 6/2019 art.22(a): the committee is appointed by RERA, not elected by owners; check your building's RERA statute.
gaps: No owners' general assembly under this law: the product's owner-meeting flow does not fit; these values describe the committee meeting only.
Appointment by a regulator rather than election is not expressible.
Other UAE emirates not covered.

packs.name: Thailand: Condominium Act B.E. 2522 (1979) - joint owners' meeting (PARTIAL)
recommended: Condominium Act s.42/1: hold the AGM within 120 days of the end of the fiscal year.
gaps: Notice, quorum, majorities and committee terms all blank: Act text not read.
